title: Headroom Manager + Burst Arbitration: PRD for proactive reserved headroom and fair burst handling for Dedicated capacity
creator: Maya Singh
description: Introduce a Headroom Manager that maintains minimal warm capacity per tenant and a Burst Arbitration system that enforces fair, preemptive, and observable burst behavior across Dedicated pools. The goal is to reduce cold-start latency for high-variance workloads while preserving isolation guarantees and predictable SLAs for reserved capacity customers.
background: Multiple customers experience intermittent latency spikes when background traffic causes GPU workloads to spin up. Existing reserve semantics are coarse (slot-level leases) and reactive; we lack a coordinated mechanism that holds small, low-cost headroom for active tenants and a transparent arbitration policy for bursts. Recent incidents (Q4 latency incidents) and numerous PM tickets requesting improved burst fairness indicate this is high priority.
goals: Reduce median p95 generation latency for tenants with unpredictable short-lived spikes by providing warm headroom that covers short bursts
Provide a configurable, auditable arbitration policy so tenants see deterministic outcomes during contention (credits, soft-fence, preemption windows)
Enable operators to set conservative defaults that maintain SLA targets for reserved pools while allowing controlled opportunistic burst behavior
Expose simple controls in Console and API for headroom sizing, burst crediting, and preemption grace so customers can tune per-tenant behavior
non_goals: Replace long-lived reserved slot semantics; reserved commitments remain the primary guarantee
Full multi-cluster live migration for tenants during bursts (out of scope for initial rollout)
Autoscaling of underlying GPU fleet — this focuses on intra-pool allocation and arbitration, not adding hardware
success_metrics: Reduce cold-start p95 latency caused by model warmup for affected tenants by >= 40% within 30 days of rollout
Maintain reserved-tenant SLA (99.9% availability and latency SLOs) for committed capacity across canary clusters
<10% increase in overall token cost for Dedicated pools when enabling default headroom (measured in first 90 days)
<1% rollback rate across customers during a staged rollout (canaries + gradual percentage ramp)
user_stories: As an SRE for a mid-market customer, I want a small guaranteed warm headroom so short chat spikes don’t incur a 2-3s model cold start
As a platform engineer at Redwood, I want clear metrics and traces showing headroom consumption and credit spend to debug customer incidents
As a product owner, I want Console toggles to set per-tenant headroom_ratio and burst_credit_policy without opening a ticket
As a flakey workload owner, I want burst credits I can accrue during low-util windows so I can use them later for controlled bursts
requirements: Headroom Manager component that tracks per-tenant warm slot reservations expressed as a minimal token of GPU capacity (configurable via headroom_ratio or min_reserved_units)
A Burst Arbitration module that implements: credit ledger per tenant, elasticity bands, preemption windows, and soft-fence enforcement
API + Console controls: headroom_ratio (0.0-1.0), min_reserved_units (integer), burst_credit_rate (tokens/sec), max_burst_multiplier, preemption_grace_secs
Fallback policies: when headroom is exhausted, requests either fall back to a compatible lower-cost model variant or queue with configurable pref/timeout
Observability: dashboards and per-tenant traces for headroom usage, credit balance, preemption events, and evictions; telemetry emitted to Console and SSO-accessible logs
Operator controls for global pool limits and emergency drain/disable of headroom feature
Integration with routing: requests are annotated with tenant_id and budget_hint so Smart Routing can factor headroom and credits into placement decisions
Policy enforcement must be deterministic and idempotent across controller restarts
Role-based UI visibility: customers can view and configure their own headroom and burst settings; operators can override for compliance-sensitive tenants
telemetry_and_observability: Per-tenant time series: headroom_reserved_units, headroom_used_units, burst_credit_balance, preemption_events_count
Export traces for allocation decisions: reason codes (preempt, fallback, credit-spend, queue), source controller, timestamps
Audit logs for configuration changes (who changed headroom/burst settings and when)
Alerting rules: sustained headroom depletion across >10% tenants in a pool -> paging; sudden spike in preemptions -> alert for potential misconfiguration
Console dashboard: heatmap of headroom utilization and top consumers over rolling 24h/7d windows
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Design review and security signoff (2 weeks): finalize policies, threat model, and data flows
Phase 1 - Implementation in staging (4 weeks): Headroom Manager + credit ledger + basic Console UI toggles; non-destructive defaults off
Phase 2 - Canary with internal customers (2 weeks): enable for 10 internal tenants across two Dedicated pools with telemetry and enforced alerts
Phase 3 - Gradual customer opt-in (6 weeks): expose toggle to customers; monitor metrics and iterate on defaults
Phase 4 - Default enable for low-risk pools (8 weeks): flip on default headroom with conservative defaults for pools tagged 'low-impact'
Phase 5 - Full rollout and hardening (ongoing): widen to all pools, tune defaults, and add automation for reclaiming stale headroom
acceptance_criteria: Automated e2e test covering headroom reservation, burst credit accrual/spend, and preemption with expected fallbacks passes in CI
Canary tenants show >= 40% reduction in cold-start p95 latency compared to baseline within 14 days
No reserved tenant SLA regressions in canary (validated by SLO dashboard and latency traces)
Operators can disable headroom globally within <5 minutes and system gracefully reclaims headroom without impacting active reserved requests
Console UI shows per-tenant credit balance and last preemption event within 60s of occurrence
Audit log entries for configuration changes are present and immutable for 90 days
open_questions: What is the minimal billing model for headroom (flat fraction of reserved commitment vs metered token usage)?
Should burst credits be transferable between tenant subaccounts or orgs? (compliance/abuse concerns)
How to reconcile headroom accounting when a tenant has cross-pool reservations spanning regions?
Is there a required hardware-level prewarm mechanism for certain GPU families to achieve target latency improvements?
Do we charge for headroom under default on-switch or only if used?
docs_and_links: Related PRD: PM-712459 (dedicated-preemptible-credit-pools-prd) - for credit semantics cross-check
notes: This PRD intentionally separates warm headroom from long-term reserved slot guarantees. Aim for conservative defaults and strong observability to avoid surprises for high-SLA customers. Plan additional experiments for billing and cross-tenant fairness after initial rollout. Work closely with Security for audit requirements and with Solutions Engineering for customer migrations.
